already-have.reason: FI-08 is the design this repo already shipped on the bench, bricked a chip with, and formally retired with a recorded "do not bring it back" rationale. The pre-2026-04-20 OPTIGA pairing flow sealed the PBS under a wrap key that mixed `measured_boot::firmware_hash()` (`secure/src/hw/huk.rs::derive_device_key`, since re-rooted) — i.e. SE access was bound to a firmware measurement. It was removed by work-todo #24 (archive line 1482 "re-rooted hw::huk::derive_device_key off firmware_hash. Done.") and the live driver comment at `secure/src/optiga/mod.rs:787-796` says the coupling "is what bricked bench units on every rebuild". The load-bearing part is not the brick but the security argument in `docs/secure-elements/optiga-brick-postmortem.md` §4 (lines 205-210): "A tampered firmware running on the legitimate MCU has the same OTP and UID access as legitimate firmware. It can compute any hash it wants and derive any wrap key … the firmware_hash-in-HUK thing was security theatre that armed a reliability bomb." The memory file `project_optiga_brick.md:26` turns that into a standing instruction: "When someone proposes mixing firmware_hash back into any SE wrap key derivation: push back hard, point at postmortem §4." FI-08 is exactly that: its proof-of-measurement key (HMAC(K_se050_meas, M) / Shielded-Connection session bound to HMAC(M)) is DHUK/BHK-derived and computed by the secure world, so any image reached via the glitched-FSBL / RDP-downgrade path it claims to defeat simply presents the expected M (it can hash the legitimate slot bytes or hard-code the digest). The SE never learns what code is running; it learns what the MCU says it measured. The proposal concedes this ("a fully compromised secure image could lie") but treats it as a corner case, when it is the entire threat it was proposed against; and it rules out the only construction that would make the measurement unforgeable ("the FSBL cannot participate"). Repo-evidence lines in the proposal are accurate (dual_se.rs:461-477 has no measurement input; measured_boot::run is advisory; secret_keys is possession-only), but "not implemented" is because it was deliberately un-implemented, not an oversight. Caveat on confidence: the postmortem/memory record is a documented design decision with a stated technical refutation, not a line tagged "owner decision — do not re-raise" in CLAUDE.md the way ML-KEM (#9) or SHAKE are; if the harness requires that exact tag, downgrade to refuted=false with the corrections below.
already-have.corrections: (1) No open issue tracks SE-bound seed release on a measurement; the nearest are #249 (work-todo #22 SLH-DSA binding manifest with firmware-hash inclusion — attestation TO the user/companion, not release gating), #210/#244 (boot-time SE attestation — the SEs prove themselves to the MCU, the opposite direction), #591/#633 (FI sweeps on fsbl::verify_images / fw_commit staging). The companion-facing "C10 MCU attestation (fingerprint-signed challenge)" half of FI-08 is genuinely untracked and does NOT contradict the postmortem — file it as its own item under #249. (2) The salvageable variant that the postmortem does not refute is a stage-keyed measurement: the WRP-frozen FSBL (invariant #10) — not the secure world — derives K_meas = KDF(stage_secret, M) and then makes stage_secret unreachable before branching (Trezor's shape: SECRET_PRIVILEGED_MASTER_KEY_SLOT in HDP-hidden flash, see mcu_attestation.c `secret_key_mcu_device_auth`; STM32U5 HDP1/2 + BHKLOCK). Only then does a wrong M yield an undecryptable half rather than a lie. That requires HDP, which production-security.md:521-528 records as deferred (ship profile HDP1EN=HDP2EN=0, verify_ship_profile has no HDP field), the FSBL to become post-secret (contradicts the current "FSBL is pre-PIN/pre-secret" model and the 40 KiB budget, #540), and a re-seal in fw_commit with the journaled old/new/KVN recovery the first-boot flow already lacks (#76/#268). If pursued, write it as a NEW proposal "FSBL stage-key sealed halves (HDP)", cite postmortem §4 as the reason the secure-world-measured version is rejected, and keep the brick lesson: every A/B update must re-seal BEFORE the boot pointer flips, atomically, or the device is a one-way brick at E140 LcsO=Operational. (3) Minor: the proposal's "Donjon Safe 3 = MCU pairing secret proves possession not code" framing matches production-security.md:707 and threat-model.md:440, which already classify that attack as harmless under the dual-SE split (single-chip break); pq1's residual is the glitched-FSBL/RDP-downgrade path, tracked as #401 (BENCH-4 RDP-2 downgrade campaign) and #301.

feasible.reason: As written, FI-08 does not defend against its own stated threat. The threat is "a glitched FSBL verify (or RDP downgrade) runs a reprogrammed secure image that still reaches both halves." The proposal then has the SECURE IMAGE compute M_current (explicitly: "the secure world recomputes M_current every boot from measured_boot::run, not the FSBL") and derive SE session material from it using DHUK/BHK roots. Bypass: the reprogrammed image simply embeds the constant M0 and never measures itself. M0 is public by design (invariant #10 requires anyone to recompute flash/option-byte/FSBL digests from the reproducible build), and the roots are available to any code on the die: the SAES DHUK selector has no HDPL-style per-stage variation on STM32U5 (that exists on STM32H5, not U5), and the BHK on pq1 is reloaded from page 126 by secure code every boot (no battery, supercap only), so `secret_keys.rs` BHK derivations are equally recomputable. The OPTIGA/SE050 never "see a measurement"; they see a key derived from (public M0, recomputable root), which is exactly the possession proof the proposal criticises. The seal adds zero bits of secret relative to today's PBS/SCP03 derivation. The risks paragraph concedes "a fully compromised secure image could lie, which is why FI-03/FI-06 remain load-bearing" — but a compromised secure image IS the threat, so the defense is empty against it. Secondary inaccuracies: a wrong OPTIGA PBS is a failed Shielded-Connection handshake (a visible refusal, not an "undecryptable half"); SE050 has no object policy that consumes an HMAC, you would just make the SCP03 static keys or an AESKey auth object the KDF output; and `measured_boot.rs` is itself the advisory row (CLAUDE.md Lifecycle), so building a release gate on it inverts the documented trust direction.
feasible.corrections: The salvageable version is measurement-KEYED handoff rooted in the FSBL, i.e. Trezor's `secret_prepare_fw` pattern (core/embed/sec/secret/stm32u5/secret.c:598-651: BHK copied to TAMP and BHKLOCKed, Optiga pairing secret cached only for trusted firmware, then `FLASH_SECHDPCR.HDP1_ACCDIS` closes the secret sector) upgraded so the handoff depends on the DIGEST rather than on the verify VERDICT: (1) a per-device secret K_hdp lives in an HDP-covered page outside the never-written FSBL range (generated by the FSBL on first boot, so the SECHDP1 range must be in the ship option-byte profile that Phase A verifies and RDP-2 freezes — a provisioning/ceremony change, so kind should be firmware+provisioning, not pure firmware); (2) the FSBL computes T = SAES-CMAC/HMAC(K_hdp, digest(branched slot) ‖ option-byte profile) BEFORE the signature check, zeroizes K_hdp, sets HDP1_ACCDIS with FI-hardened read-back, and leaves T in SRAM; (3) the secure world mixes T into the PBS/SCP03 derivations. A glitched verify then branches into code holding a wrong T it cannot repair; Trezor's design, by contrast, hands the secret over on a single boolean. Remaining limits: a glitch that skips HDP1_ACCDIS, or a glitch that hashes slot B while branching to slot A, must be covered by FSBL FI-hardening (bind the hash range and the branch target to the same sentinel); a successful RDP downgrade still wins (a debugger halts before ACCDIS and reads K_hdp), so FI-03/FI-06 stay load-bearing; the FSBL becomes secret-bearing, contradicting the current "FSBL is pre-secret" framing and widening the WRP/HDP ceremony that invariant #10 already lists as OPEN; fw_update must re-wrap the SE-side credentials under the new T before the boot pointer flips, with the same journaled old/new recovery proof the first-boot flow still lacks (brick risk is real); FSBL budget is 28,704 B LOAD of 38,912 B, so a CMAC + flash-write path fits but must be re-gated by `make fsbl`. Cost L is right for the corrected design; the design as written should not be scheduled at all, and the corrected one is P2 only after the HDP range is part of the approved option-byte ceremony. Also: "the SEs saw the expected measurement" is never literally true — the SE sees a key; honesty requires stating that the trust anchor becomes "the FSBL+HDP measured the branched slot", not the SE.
